title: Sensex Crashes 813 Points as $100 Oil and West Asia Tensions Rattle Markets
excerpt: The benchmark fell for a third straight session to 74,764 as Brent crude topped $100 and IT stocks led a broad selloff; India VIX jumped over 6%.
body:
• The BSE Sensex crashed 813.35 points (1.08%) to 74,764.23 on Wednesday — its third straight day of declines — while the Nifty fell below 23,450.
  • Escalating US-Iran tensions pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel for the first time in nearly six weeks, rattling sentiment across Asia.
  • IT stocks led the selloff: HCL Tech dropped 4.55%, with Infosys, TCS and Tech Mahindra among the major laggards; India VIX jumped over 6%.
  • Foreign investors sold ₹123.19 crore in equities on Tuesday, extending the risk-off mood in Indian markets.

Indian equities extended their slide for a third consecutive session on Wednesday, with the benchmark Sensex tumbling 813.35 points as escalating tensions in West Asia drove crude oil above $100 a barrel and deepened a broad risk-off mood.

The 30-share BSE Sensex sank 1.08% to settle at the day's low of 74,764.23, according to The Hindu. The 50-share NSE Nifty declined 203.60 points, or 0.86%, to end at 23,431.50.

Oil shock meets IT selloff

The proximate trigger was energy. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, jumped 2.67% to $100.5 a barrel after attacks on oil facilities and ships in West Asia threatened an already strained supply chain. For India, which imports the bulk of its crude, $100 oil is an inflation and current-account warning in one.

Technology stocks bore the brunt of the selling. Among the 30 Sensex constituents, HCL Technologies dropped the most at 4.55%. Infosys, Tech Mahindra, Tata Consultancy Services, HDFC Bank and Hindustan Unilever were also among the major laggards. Defensive buying showed up selectively: Adani Ports, Tata Steel, Trent and NTPC ended among the winners.

"Elevated crude oil prices, lingering geopolitical tensions and a sharp rise in market volatility continued to weigh on investor confidence, reinforcing the market's prevailing bearish undertone."

— Ponmudi R, CEO, Enrich Money

Volatility surges

Fear gauges flashed amber. The India VIX — the market's volatility index — climbed more than 6%, reflecting increased hedging activity and growing caution over the near-term outlook, Ponmudi said.

The weakness was not India's alone. In Asia, South Korea's Kospi and Shanghai's SSE Composite ended higher, but Japan's Nikkei 225 and Hong Kong's Hang Seng settled lower. European markets were trading in the red, and US markets had ended Tuesday in negative territory. Foreign Institutional Investors offloaded equities worth ₹123.19 crore on Tuesday, exchange data showed, adding to the selling pressure.

Three days of damage

Wednesday's fall capped a bruising stretch. On Tuesday, the Sensex had dropped 555.23 points to 75,577.58 and the Nifty 144.05 points to 23,635.10. The proximate geopolitical driver: the US military destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to attacks on its warships, and Iran hit back at American targets in Jordan — an escalation cycle that has energy markets on edge.

What investors should watch

For NRI portfolios with India exposure, the near-term calculus is straightforward: crude above $100 squeezes corporate margins, pressures the rupee and raises the odds of sticky inflation — all headwinds for equities. Analysts say the market's direction now hinges less on domestic earnings and more on whether the US-Iran confrontation stabilises or spirals. Until crude cools, rallies are likely to be sold.
